mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a tight labor market with strong job growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector is a key component of the economy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it indicates an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased consumer spending supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS shows positive growth for two consecutive months.
